scene.label: Act 5, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. Padua. Before Lucentio's house.

content.text: Enter on one side Biondello, Lucentio and Bianca; Gremio walking on other side.

lines.text: Softly and swiftly, sir, for the priest is ready.
lines.plainText: Softly and swiftly sir for the priest is ready

lines.text: I fly, Biondello; but they may chance to need thee at home, therefore leave us.
lines.plainText: I fly Biondello but they may chance to need thee at home therefore leave us

lines.text: Nay, faith, I'll see the church o' your back; and then come back to my master's as soon as I can.
lines.plainText: Nay faith I'll see the church o' your back and then come back to my master's as soon as I can

lines.text: I marvel Cambio comes not all this while.
lines.plainText: I marvel Cambio comes not all this while

content.text: Enter Petruchio, Katherina, Vincentio and Attendants.

lines.text: Sir, here's the door; this is Lucentio's house:
lines.plainText: Sir here's the door this is Lucentio's house

lines.text: My father's bears more toward the market-place;
lines.plainText: My father's bears more toward the marketplace

lines.text: Thither must I, and here I leave you, sir.
lines.plainText: Thither must I and here I leave you sir

lines.text: You shall not choose but drink before you go.
lines.plainText: You shall not choose but drink before you go

lines.text: I think I shall command your welcome here,
lines.plainText: I think I shall command your welcome here

lines.text: And by all likelihood some cheer is toward.
lines.plainText: And by all likelihood some cheer is toward

lines.text: They're busy within; you were best knock louder.
lines.plainText: They're busy within you were best knock louder

content.text: Enter Pedant above, at a window.

lines.text: What's he that knocks as he would beat down the gate?
lines.plainText: What's he that knocks as he would beat down the gate

lines.text: Is Signior Lucentio within, sir?
lines.plainText: Is Signior Lucentio within sir

lines.text: He's within, sir, but not to be spoken withal.
lines.plainText: He's within sir but not to be spoken withal

lines.text: What if a man bring him a hundred pound or two to make merry withal?
lines.plainText: What if a man bring him a hundred pound or two to make merry withal

lines.text: Keep your hundred pounds to yourself: he shall need none so long as I live.
lines.plainText: Keep your hundred pounds to yourself he shall need none so long as I live

lines.text: Nay, I told you your son was well beloved in Padua. Do you hear, sir? To leave frivolous circumstances, I pray you tell Signior Lucentio that his father is come from Pisa, and is here at the door to speak with him.
lines.plainText: Nay I told you your son was well beloved in Padua Do you hear sir To leave frivolous circumstances I pray you tell Signior Lucentio that his father is come from Pisa and is here at the door to speak with him

lines.text: Thou liest: his father is come from Padua, and here looking out at the window.
lines.plainText: Thou liest his father is come from Padua and here looking out at the window

lines.text: Art thou his father?
lines.plainText: Art thou his father

lines.text: Ay, sir; so his mother says, if I may believe her.
lines.plainText: Ay sir so his mother says if I may believe her

lines.text: [To Vincentio] Why, how now, gentleman! why, this is flat knavery to take upon you another man's name.
lines.plainText: To Vincentio Why how now gentleman why this is flat knavery to take upon you another man's name

lines.text: Lay hands on the villain: I believe a means to cozen somebody in this city under my countenance.
lines.plainText: Lay hands on the villain I believe a means to cozen somebody in this city under my countenance

lines.text: I have seen them in the church together: God send 'em good shipping! But who is here? Mine old master, Vincentio! Now we are undone and brought to nothing.
lines.plainText: I have seen them in the church together God send 'em good shipping But who is here Mine old master Vincentio Now we are undone and brought to nothing

lines.text: [Seeing Biondello.] Come hither, crack-hemp.
lines.plainText: Seeing Biondello Come hither crackhemp

lines.text: I hope I may choose, sir.
lines.plainText: I hope I may choose sir

lines.text: Come hither, you rogue. What, have you forgot me?
lines.plainText: Come hither you rogue What have you forgot me

lines.text: Forgot you! No, sir: I could not forget you, for I never saw you before in all my life.
lines.plainText: Forgot you No sir I could not forget you for I never saw you before in all my life

lines.text: What, you notorious villain! didst thou never see thy master's father, Vincentio?
lines.plainText: What you notorious villain didst thou never see thy master's father Vincentio

lines.text: What, my old worshipful old master? Yes, marry, sir; see where he looks out of the window.
lines.plainText: What my old worshipful old master Yes marry sir see where he looks out of the window

lines.text: Is't so, indeed?
lines.plainText: Is't so indeed

lines.text: Help, help, help! here's a madman will murder me.
lines.plainText: Help help help here's a madman will murder me

lines.text: Help, son! help, Signior Baptista!
lines.plainText: Help son help Signior Baptista

lines.text: Prithee, Kate, let's stand aside and see the end of this controversy.
lines.plainText: Prithee Kate let's stand aside and see the end of this controversy

content.text: Re-enter Pedant, below; Baptista, Tranio and Servants.

lines.text: Sir, what are you that offer to beat my servant?
lines.plainText: Sir what are you that offer to beat my servant

lines.text: What am I, sir! nay, what are you, sir? O immortal gods! O fine villain! A silken doublet, a velvet hose, a scarlet cloak, and a copatain hat! O, I am undone! I am undone! While I play the good husband at home, my son and my servant spend all at the university.
lines.plainText: What am I sir nay what are you sir O immortal gods O fine villain A silken doublet a velvet hose a scarlet cloak and a copatain hat O I am undone I am undone While I play the good husband at home my son and my servant spend all at the university

lines.text: How now! what's the matter?
lines.plainText: How now what's the matter

lines.text: What, is the man lunatic?
lines.plainText: What is the man lunatic

lines.text: Sir, you seem a sober ancient gentleman by your habit, but your words show you a madman. Why, sir, what 'cerns it you if I wear pearl and gold? I thank my good father, I am able to maintain it.
lines.plainText: Sir you seem a sober ancient gentleman by your habit but your words show you a madman Why sir what 'cerns it you if I wear pearl and gold I thank my good father I am able to maintain it

lines.text: Thy father! O villain! he is a sailmaker in Bergamo.
lines.plainText: Thy father O villain he is a sailmaker in Bergamo

lines.text: You mistake, sir; you mistake, sir. Pray, what do you think is his name?
lines.plainText: You mistake sir you mistake sir Pray what do you think is his name

lines.text: His name! As if I knew not his name! I have brought him up ever since he was three years old, and his name is Tranio.
lines.plainText: His name As if I knew not his name I have brought him up ever since he was three years old and his name is Tranio

lines.text: Away, away, mad ass! His name is Lucentio; and he is mine only son, and heir to the lands of me, Signior Vincentio.
lines.plainText: Away away mad ass His name is Lucentio and he is mine only son and heir to the lands of me Signior Vincentio

lines.text: Lucentio! O, he hath murdered his master! Lay hold on him, I charge you, in the Duke's name. O, my son, my son! Tell me, thou villain, where is my son, Lucentio?
lines.plainText: Lucentio O he hath murdered his master Lay hold on him I charge you in the Duke's name O my son my son Tell me thou villain where is my son Lucentio

lines.text: Call forth an officer.
lines.plainText: Call forth an officer

lines.text: Carry me to the gaol!
lines.plainText: Carry me to the gaol

lines.text: Stay, officer; he shall not go to prison.
lines.plainText: Stay officer he shall not go to prison

lines.text: Talk not, Signior Gremio; I say he shall go to prison.
lines.plainText: Talk not Signior Gremio I say he shall go to prison

lines.text: Take heed, Signior Baptista, lest you be cony-catched in this business; I dare swear this is the right Vincentio.
lines.plainText: Take heed Signior Baptista lest you be conycatched in this business I dare swear this is the right Vincentio

lines.text: Swear if thou darest.
lines.plainText: Swear if thou darest

lines.text: Nay, I dare not swear it.
lines.plainText: Nay I dare not swear it

lines.text: Then thou wert best say that I am not Lucentio.
lines.plainText: Then thou wert best say that I am not Lucentio

lines.text: Yes, I know thee to be Signior Lucentio.
lines.plainText: Yes I know thee to be Signior Lucentio

lines.text: Away with the dotard! to the gaol with him!
lines.plainText: Away with the dotard to the gaol with him

lines.text: Thus strangers may be haled and abus'd: O monstrous villain!
lines.plainText: Thus strangers may be haled and abus'd O monstrous villain

content.text: Re-enter Biondello, with Lucentio and Bianca.

lines.text: O! we are spoiled; and yonder he is: deny him, forswear him, or else we are all undone.
lines.plainText: O we are spoiled and yonder he is deny him forswear him or else we are all undone

lines.text: [Kneeling.] Pardon, sweet father.
lines.plainText: Kneeling Pardon sweet father

lines.text: Lives my sweetest son?
lines.plainText: Lives my sweetest son

lines.text: [Kneeling.] Pardon, dear father.
lines.plainText: Kneeling Pardon dear father

lines.text: How hast thou offended?
lines.plainText: How hast thou offended

lines.text: Where is Lucentio?
lines.plainText: Where is Lucentio

lines.text: Here's Lucentio,
lines.plainText: Here's Lucentio

lines.text: Right son to the right Vincentio;
lines.plainText: Right son to the right Vincentio

lines.text: That have by marriage made thy daughter mine,
lines.plainText: That have by marriage made thy daughter mine

lines.text: While counterfeit supposes blear'd thine eyne.
lines.plainText: While counterfeit supposes blear'd thine eyne

lines.text: Here 's packing, with a witness, to deceive us all!
lines.plainText: Here 's packing with a witness to deceive us all

lines.text: Where is that damned villain, Tranio,
lines.plainText: Where is that damned villain Tranio

lines.text: That fac'd and brav'd me in this matter so?
lines.plainText: That fac'd and brav'd me in this matter so

lines.text: Why, tell me, is not this my Cambio?
lines.plainText: Why tell me is not this my Cambio

lines.text: Cambio is chang'd into Lucentio.
lines.plainText: Cambio is chang'd into Lucentio

lines.text: Love wrought these miracles. Bianca's love
lines.plainText: Love wrought these miracles Bianca's love

lines.text: Made me exchange my state with Tranio,
lines.plainText: Made me exchange my state with Tranio

lines.text: While he did bear my countenance in the town;
lines.plainText: While he did bear my countenance in the town

lines.text: And happily I have arriv'd at the last
lines.plainText: And happily I have arriv'd at the last

lines.text: Unto the wished haven of my bliss.
lines.plainText: Unto the wished haven of my bliss

lines.text: What Tranio did, myself enforc'd him to;
lines.plainText: What Tranio did myself enforc'd him to

lines.text: Then pardon him, sweet father, for my sake.
lines.plainText: Then pardon him sweet father for my sake

lines.text: I'll slit the villain's nose that would have sent me to the gaol.
lines.plainText: I'll slit the villain's nose that would have sent me to the gaol

lines.text: [To Lucentio.] But do you hear, sir? Have you married my daughter without asking my good will?
lines.plainText: To Lucentio But do you hear sir Have you married my daughter without asking my good will

lines.text: Fear not, Baptista; we will content you, go to: but I will in, to be revenged for this villainy.
lines.plainText: Fear not Baptista we will content you go to but I will in to be revenged for this villainy

lines.text: And I to sound the depth of this knavery.
lines.plainText: And I to sound the depth of this knavery

lines.text: Look not pale, Bianca; thy father will not frown.
lines.plainText: Look not pale Bianca thy father will not frown

lines.text: My cake is dough, but I'll in among the rest;
lines.plainText: My cake is dough but I'll in among the rest

lines.text: Out of hope of all but my share of the feast.
lines.plainText: Out of hope of all but my share of the feast

lines.text: Husband, let's follow to see the end of this ado.
lines.plainText: Husband let's follow to see the end of this ado

lines.text: First kiss me, Kate, and we will.
lines.plainText: First kiss me Kate and we will

lines.text: What! in the midst of the street?
lines.plainText: What in the midst of the street

lines.text: What! art thou ashamed of me?
lines.plainText: What art thou ashamed of me

lines.text: No, sir; God forbid; but ashamed to kiss.
lines.plainText: No sir God forbid but ashamed to kiss

lines.text: Why, then, let's home again. Come, sirrah, let's away.
lines.plainText: Why then let's home again Come sirrah let's away

lines.text: Nay, I will give thee a kiss: now pray thee, love, stay.
lines.plainText: Nay I will give thee a kiss now pray thee love stay

lines.text: Is not this well? Come, my sweet Kate:
lines.plainText: Is not this well Come my sweet Kate

lines.text: Better once than never, for never too late.
lines.plainText: Better once than never for never too late
